title: People are asking agents to strip the smart TV. Experts say use the settings.
friendlyTitle: People are asking AI to simplify their smart TVs. Experts say start with the settings.
summary: CBC reports that viral posts are showing people how to ask a coding agent to remove apps, ads, and some tracking from a smart TV, after the set becomes slow or noisy. Toronto analyst Ritesh Kotak and London, Ontario journalist Carmi Levy say the same job can often be done in the TV's own settings, or by leaving the television offline and putting the apps on a separate streaming stick. They also say an agent-written change can brick the set, void the warranty, or skip the security updates that a connected TV still needs. One person told CBC-cited posts that an attempt left an Android TV unusable.

whyItMatters: The useful part is the complaint, not the prompt. If the TV is collecting data and showing ads you did not ask for, the safer first move is the settings menu, or a stick that is the only thing on the network. An agent that rewrites the set while it stays online can remove the updates that were there to patch it. This is a product problem people are trying to solve with a coding agent. It is not a recipe.
